Definition: from a compound of G1909 and G1218; to make oneself at home, i.e. (by extension) to reside (in a foreign country):--(be) dwelling (which were) there, stranger.
BiblicalUsage: Epidemeo means to reside as a stranger, to make oneself at home in a foreign place. Dwellers in Mesopotamia and strangers of Rome were at Pentecost; and the Athenians spent their time in nothing else but to tell or to hear some new thing.
TheologicalSignificance: The Christian's position is at home nowhere on earth for long, and always listening — the question is what we are listening for.
